title: After Hours
excerpt: Erotic office romance · Forbidden attraction · Workplace drama
content:
Victoria arrived at work determined to restore order.

She greeted Daniel with a professional nod, assigned him three reports, and avoided looking at him for longer than necessary.

He followed her instructions without complaint.

Somehow, his silence was worse than his teasing.

At eleven, their director called an emergency meeting and demanded a revised proposal before the following morning. By six, the department had emptied, leaving Victoria and Daniel alone with two laptops, a stack of documents, and a deadline that seemed increasingly impossible.

"Take a break," Daniel suggested.

"We don't have time."

"You've read that same paragraph four times."

Victoria rubbed her forehead. "I have a deadline."

"And I have two working hands. Let me handle the final section."

She looked at him. "You know what? Fine. I'll review your work afterward."

"That's what supervisors are for."

She almost smiled.

They worked until the rain returned, heavier this time. At nine-thirty, Victoria leaned back in her chair and closed her eyes.

"Done," Daniel announced.

She opened them. "Already?"

"Finished, checked, and formatted."

She reviewed the document. It was excellent.

"Daniel, this is genuinely good work."

"Careful. Compliments might go to my head."

"Don't ruin the moment."

He laughed, and she found herself laughing with him.

For a few minutes, they weren't supervisor and intern. They were simply two people sharing a quiet office after a difficult day.

Daniel walked over to collect the printed pages. Victoria stood at the same moment, and they nearly collided.

His hand caught her elbow.

"You okay?"

"Yes."

He didn't immediately release her, but his grip remained gentle.

Victoria looked up. His face was closer than she expected.

"You're making this difficult," she whispered.

"I know."

"You work for me."

"I know that too."

"If anything happens, it could affect your internship."

"Then we don't have to do anything."

His answer surprised her.

He stepped back, giving her room to decide.

Victoria had spent years being the person who made every decision, who anticipated every problem, who never allowed herself to want something she couldn't control.

Now, she wanted to close the distance between them.

She put the papers down.

"Daniel, if we're going to discuss this, we need to be honest. You cannot feel pressured to please me because I'm your supervisor."

"I'm not pressured," he said. "And I don't want you to think you owe me anything either."

She searched his expression.

"You're certain?"

"Absolutely."

Victoria reached for his hand.

He looked down at their joined fingers, then back at her.

"Is this still a professional conversation?" he asked.

"Not remotely."

He smiled.

She kissed him first.

It began cautiously, almost as if either of them could still pretend it was a mistake. But when they drew apart, neither moved away.

Daniel touched her cheek. "Tell me if you want me to stop."

"I will."

She kissed him again.

This time, the restraint between them broke—not into a reckless rush, but into weeks of curiosity finally given permission to exist. They kissed beside her desk, laughing breathlessly when a stack of papers slid to the floor.

Victoria pulled away just enough to look at him.

"We are absolutely terrible at maintaining professional boundaries."

"Speak for yourself," he murmured. "I've been trying to impress you professionally for weeks."

She laughed and rested her forehead against his.

For a moment, the office outside their little world ceased to matter.

Then Victoria's eyes caught the clock.

The reality returned.

She stepped back, straightened her blouse, and took a steadying breath.

"We need to think about what happens tomorrow."

Daniel nodded. "Then let's think about it properly. No secrets that put either of us in a bad position."

She appreciated that more than he knew.

"I'll speak to HR about changing your reporting arrangement," she said. "Until that's sorted, we keep things professional at work."

"Agreed."

He gathered his things.

At the elevator, he turned around.

"Victoria?"

"Yes?"

"Tonight wasn't a mistake to me."

She held his gaze.

"Neither was it to me."

The elevator doors closed.

Victoria stood alone in the office, her heart beating too quickly for someone who had spent years believing she had everything under control.

She didn't regret the kiss.

What frightened her was how much she wanted another one.
